title: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever
synopsis: A device built by an MIT student can locate vibranium. Namor wants its inventor killed to protect Talokan. Shuri and Ramonda offer Riri protection as Wakanda mourns its king.
verdictRationale: Riri has no army and little say in what others do with her invention. Shuri’s refusal to surrender her is a reason to admire the princess. Grief also makes retaliation tempting. The story invites sympathy for that struggle while framing it through encounters with ancestors and Wakandan deities that call for discernment.
ageRationale: A drowning and two family bereavements give the battles lasting consequences. A child grieving someone close may find the quiet beach scene harder than the combat.
reflection: Shuri once bargains for her brother’s life. On the beach she finally allows herself to grieve him. An Orthodox family might remember someone by name in prayer and leave room for the person who finds it hard to speak.

title: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3
synopsis: Rocket is gravely wounded, and a device inside him prevents ordinary treatment. His friends search for the code that will let them help him. Flashbacks show why that device is there.
verdictRationale: The High Evolutionary values creatures according to how well they fit his design. Rocket’s friends risk themselves for someone who cannot repay them. When Drax stays to care for the rescued children, the story gives ordinary, lasting care the same dignity as the rescue.
ageRationale: Experiments on frightened animals, a mutilated face and the destruction of an inhabited world can be especially distressing. Strong profanity and a prolonged portrayal of animal suffering inform the older-teen recommendation.
reflection: Drax has spent years being praised for what he can destroy. On Knowhere the children need someone who will stay. A gift can become clear when someone asks who needs us tomorrow, after the emergency has passed.
